page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-2 is an entry-level compute-optimized instance belonging to the E2 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled at 2 threads per core. It includes 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the e2-highcpu-2 in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1105.98, while the multi-core score is 1452.89. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 13.03 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 11.11 GB/sec. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 906.0 and a multi-core score of 1073.0. For specialized tasks, the instance achieves a static web serving throughput of 1.39 GB/sec and an LLM inference text generation speed of 64.17 tokens/sec for a small 135M model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require substantial memory capacity. The primary tradeoff is its low overall resource density and constrained memory, which limits its capability to handle memory-intensive applications or heavy concurrent processing. This server is best suited for lightweight, compute-oriented tasks such as basic web serving, simple text processing, software compilation with low memory requirements, and small-scale utility scripting.
